Q: Jekyll compiling seems WAY too slow A:

Editorial Note: the node_modules directory is excluded by default since Jekyll 4 was released in 2019. See other answers for solutions for Jekyll 4+.

I ran into a similar problem, but I luckily found the reason and a solution:

My Jekyll setup wasn't using any plugins, no complicated liquid tags, only contained three sample posts and nothing else. But building the site still took 6 seconds on average.

Only when I removed everything in the directory step by step, I found out what was causing the long build times: the node_modules folder.

You can exclude the node_modules directory from the Jekyll conversion by putting the following in the _config.yml file:

exclude: [node_modules]

Or:

exclude:
    - node_modules

More information about exclude can be found in the Jekyll documentation.

Q: Anaconda installation stuck at "Setting up package cache.." A:

In my case, I saw in the task manager under Conda processes, two CDM stuck tasks, I closed both of them and the installation continued with no issues.

Q: How to POST a string HttpContent to ASP.net Core web API? A:

Looking at your AddMore method. I think you should also get the body content using the [FromBody] string parameter as well, I do not see it specified.

Note also if you do not specify accept/content type it is by default application/json in .NET core

P.S Also consider making your AddMore method an async method

Q: Disable NonZeroResultCode status details in Rundeck notification on job failure A:

You can force the "exit 0" in your step wrapping it on some inline script like this

#!/bin/bash

touch /root/test 2> /dev/null

if [ $? -eq 1 ]
then
  # whatever you want
  echo "Successfully created file"
  exit 0
else
  echo "Could not create file" >&2
  exit 1
fi
